hypothesis: Selecting distinct provider-symbol mechanisms for long and short exposure may produce a stronger bidirectional shared-capital portfolio than requiring every provider route to work symmetrically on both sides.
decision: Retain the report-only separate-side research frontier and the unchanged armed v25 runtime, but supersede revision 1's ambiguous profit-factor label. Mixed-profile ranking uses return-on-entry-margin-normalized profit factor, while ordinary USD profit factor is now published separately. HYPE HT-Breakout long remains the only repeated-positive mixed-profile component: eight closes, five wins, three losses, +$0.502458 net, USD profit factor 1.304540, normalized profit factor 3.079128, and median return on entry margin 1.593411%. Its positive economics remain descriptive because they span incompatible profile generations and conflict with adverse historical route-shape evidence. HYPE HT-Breakout short remains adverse: four closes, one win, three losses, -$1.254625 net, USD profit factor 0.156335, and normalized profit factor 0.469534. No strategy, route, position, size, gate, exit, protection, or live process changed.
falsifier: This revision is invalidated by evidence hash or scope drift, a generic profit_factor field reappearing in the schema-v2 side-composition economics, normalized and USD denominators being pooled, side counts or net PnL failing to reconcile with the source audit, or any report-only code changing runtime state. HYPE-long priority would weaken if additional compatible closes make either its net PnL or median return on margin nonpositive, or if shared-capital interaction replay shows its standalone contribution is consumed by overlap and costs. The weak-short assessment would update after repeated independent after-friction short lifecycles.
limitations: All-live history combines materially different strategy profiles and does not establish current-v25 route edge.
The current audit is a live prefix with three provisional open positions, so evidence_complete is false.
HYPE HT-Breakout long has no compatible current-v25 close and conflicts with adverse historical route-shape evidence.
The only repeated-positive component has eight closes; that is descriptive rather than statistically durable evidence.
USD profit factor weights trades by dollar PnL, while normalized profit factor gives each trade's return on entry margin its own contribution; neither denominator is universally superior.
Standalone component ranking does not model simultaneous signals, slot contention, correlated exposure, shared-capital path dependence, or missed opportunity cost.
The report does not estimate an allocator, portfolio drawdown distribution, or future profit.
No live route, position, order, stop, target, size, exit, transition drain, or protection changed in this revision.
